subject: maths
title: Year 6 Estimation and Financial Problems
seo_title: Year 6 Estimation and Financial Maths Worksheets: Free with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Approximate numerical solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts, using appropriate estimation strategies
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on estimation and financial problems, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N08): round decimals, estimate with decimals, estimate percentages and discounts, check if answers are reasonable, and solve budget, saving and best-buy problems with unit prices. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Round to friendly numbers, then calculate: 25% of $79 is about 25% of $80 = $20.
key_sub: To find the best buy, compare the price of the same amount, such as the price per 100 g. Always check an exact answer against your estimate.
body_html:
Round first, then estimate

An estimate is a quick answer that is close to the exact answer. Round the numbers to friendly numbers, then work it out in your head. To round a decimal, look only at the digit just after the place you round to. 5 or more rounds up; 4 or less rounds down.

Estimate with decimals

Estimate 6.8 × 4.1.

6.8 rounds to 7 and 4.1 rounds to 4. 7 × 4 = 28. (The exact answer is 27.88.)

Answer: about 28

Estimating percentages

Change the percentage into a friendly fraction, and round the amount so it is easy to divide.

PercentageFractionHow to find itExample
50%one halfdivide by 250% of $198 ≈ $200 ÷ 2 = $100
25%one quarterdivide by 425% of $79 ≈ $80 ÷ 4 = $20
10%one tenthdivide by 1010% of $61 ≈ $60 ÷ 10 = $6
20%two tenthsfind 10%, then double20% of $148 ≈ 2 × $15 = $30
5%half of 10%find 10%, then halve5% of $199 ≈ $20 ÷ 2 = $10
A sale

A $59.95 jacket is 30% off. About how much is the sale price?

$59.95 is about $60. 10% of $60 is $6, so 30% is $18. $60 − $18 = $42.

Answer: about $42

Best buys and budgets

To find the best buy, compare the price of the same amount, such as 100 g or 1 kg. Australian supermarkets show this unit price on the shelf label.

Is it reasonable?

Kai works out 5.1 × 3.9 and gets 198.9.

Estimate: 5 × 4 = 20. 198.9 is about 10 times too big, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 19.89.

Answer: not reasonable

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding the wrong place: 15.49 → 15.5 → 16Look only at the tenths digit: 15.49 rounds to 15
Writing 9.96 to one decimal place as 9.1010 tenths make 1 whole: 9.96 rounds to 10.0
Estimating too far away: 6.8 × 4.1 ≈ 6 × 4 = 24Round to the nearest whole number: 7 × 4 = 28
25% of $79 ≈ $79 − $25 = $5425% is one quarter: $80 ÷ 4 = $20
Ignoring units: comparing $7.50 for 1 kg with $6.00 for 750 g by price onlyChange to the same unit and compare the price per 100 g

faq.q: What does Year 6 learn about estimation in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 6 students approximate answers to problems with decimals, fractions and percentages, including money problems, using estimation strategies that suit the problem (AC9M6N08).

faq.q: How do you estimate a percentage of an amount?
faq.a: Round the amount to a friendly number and use a benchmark percentage: 50% is half, 25% is a quarter and 10% is a tenth. For 25% of $79, use $80 ÷ 4 = $20.

faq.q: How do you find the best buy using the unit price?
faq.a: Work out the price of the same amount for each item, such as the price per 100 g, and choose the lowest. Australian supermarkets show this unit price on the shelf label.

faq.q: How can my child check if a decimal answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Round each number to the nearest whole number and work out an estimate in your head. If 4.9 × 6.1 gives 298.9 but 5 × 6 = 30, the decimal point is in the wrong place.

items.q: Round 4.62 to a whole number.
items.e: 4.62 is between 4 and 5. Look only at the tenths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 5.

items.q: Round 7.38 to a whole number.
items.e: 7.38 is between 7 and 8. Look only at the tenths digit: 3. It is 4 or less, so round down to 7.

items.q: Round 12.5 to a whole number.
items.e: 12.5 is between 12 and 13. Look only at the tenths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 13.

items.q: Round 15.49 to a whole number.
items.e: 15.49 is between 15 and 16. Look only at the tenths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 15. Do not round twice (15.49 → 15.5 → 16).

items.q: Round 39.6 to a whole number.
items.e: 39.6 is between 39 and 40. Look only at the tenths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 40.

items.q: Round 0.83 to a whole number.
items.e: 0.83 is between 0 and 1. Look only at the tenths digit: 8. It is 5 or more, so round up to 1.

items.q: Round 6.507 to a whole number.
items.e: 6.507 is between 6 and 7. Look only at the tenths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 7.

items.q: Round 23.09 to a whole number.
items.e: 23.09 is between 23 and 24. Look only at the tenths digit: 0. It is 4 or less, so round down to 23.

items.q: Round 48.45 kg to the nearest kilogram.
items.e: 48.45 kg is between 48 kg and 49 kg. Look only at the tenths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 48 kg. Do not round twice (48.45 → 48.5 → 49).

items.q: Round 2.7 L to the nearest litre.
items.e: 2.7 L is between 2 L and 3 L. Look only at the tenths digit: 7. It is 5 or more, so round up to 3 L.

items.q: Round 3.46 to one decimal place.
items.e: 3.46 is between 3.4 and 3.5. Look only at the hundredths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 3.5.

items.q: Round 8.72 to one decimal place.
items.e: 8.72 is between 8.7 and 8.8. Look only at the hundredths digit: 2. It is 4 or less, so round down to 8.7.

items.q: Round 5.35 to one decimal place.
items.e: 5.35 is between 5.3 and 5.4. Look only at the hundredths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 5.4.

items.q: Round 2.049 to one decimal place.
items.e: 2.049 is between 2.0 and 2.1. Look only at the hundredths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 2.0. Do not round twice (2.049 → 2.05 → 2.1).

items.q: Round 9.96 to one decimal place.
items.e: 9.96 is between 9.9 and 10.0. Look only at the hundredths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 10.0. One more tenth than 9.9 is 10.0 (10 tenths make 1 whole).

items.q: Round 14.682 to one decimal place.
items.e: 14.682 is between 14.6 and 14.7. Look only at the hundredths digit: 8. It is 5 or more, so round up to 14.7.

items.q: Round 0.374 to one decimal place.
items.e: 0.374 is between 0.3 and 0.4. Look only at the hundredths digit: 7. It is 5 or more, so round up to 0.4.

items.q: Round 6.95 to one decimal place.
items.e: 6.95 is between 6.9 and 7.0. Look only at the hundredths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 7.0. One more tenth than 6.9 is 7.0 (10 tenths make 1 whole).

items.q: Round 11.14 m to one decimal place.
items.e: 11.14 m is between 11.1 m and 11.2 m. Look only at the hundredths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 11.1 m.

items.q: Round 3.351 kg to one decimal place.
items.e: 3.351 kg is between 3.3 kg and 3.4 kg. Look only at the hundredths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 3.4 kg.

items.q: Estimate 4.8 + 7.3 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 5 + 7 = 12. (The exact answer is 12.1.)

items.q: Estimate 12.65 + 6.4 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 13 + 6 = 19. (The exact answer is 19.05.)

items.q: Estimate 15.62 − 8.9 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 16 − 9 = 7. (The exact answer is 6.72.)

items.q: Estimate 23.4 − 9.75 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 23 − 10 = 13. (The exact answer is 13.65.)

items.q: Estimate 3.71 + 5.48 + 8.2 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 4 + 5 + 8 = 17. (The exact answer is 17.39.)

items.q: Estimate 31.18 + 17.6 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 31 + 18 = 49. (The exact answer is 48.78.)

items.q: Estimate 6.8 × 4 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 6.8 rounds to 7. 7 × 4 = 28. (The exact answer is 27.2.)

items.q: Estimate 7.2 × 8 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 7.2 rounds to 7. 7 × 8 = 56. (The exact answer is 57.6.)

items.q: Estimate 9.85 × 6 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 9.85 rounds to 10. 10 × 6 = 60. (The exact answer is 59.1.)

items.q: Estimate 3.9 × 5.1 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 3.9 rounds to 4 and 5.1 rounds to 5. 4 × 5 = 20. (The exact answer is 19.89.)

items.q: Estimate 4.6 × 2.3 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 4.6 rounds to 5 and 2.3 rounds to 2. 5 × 2 = 10. (The exact answer is 10.58.)

items.q: Estimate 12.4 × 3.8 by rounding to whole numbers.
items.e: 12.4 rounds to 12 and 3.8 rounds to 4. 12 × 4 = 48. (The exact answer is 47.12.)

items.q: Use a compatible number to estimate 23.7 ÷ 6.
items.e: 23.7 is close to 24, and 24 ÷ 6 = 4 exactly. So 23.7 ÷ 6 is about 4. (The exact answer is 3.95.)

items.q: Use a compatible number to estimate 41.6 ÷ 7.
items.e: 41.6 is close to 42, and 42 ÷ 7 = 6 exactly. So 41.6 ÷ 7 is about 6. (The exact answer is about 5.94.)

items.q: Use a compatible number to estimate 63.5 ÷ 8.
items.e: 63.5 is close to 64, and 64 ÷ 8 = 8 exactly. So 63.5 ÷ 8 is about 8. (The exact answer is about 7.94.)

items.q: Estimate 0.48 × 62.
items.e: 0.48 is close to 0.5, which is one half. Half of 60 is 30. (The exact answer is 29.76.)

items.q: Estimate 0.26 × 81.
items.e: 0.26 is close to 0.25, which is one quarter. A quarter of 80 is 20. (The exact answer is 21.06.)

items.q: Estimate 0.49 × 398.
items.e: 0.49 is close to 0.5. Half of 400 is 200. (The exact answer is 195.02.)

items.q: Estimate 0.11 × 59.
items.e: 0.11 is close to 0.1, which is one tenth. One tenth of 60 is 6. (The exact answer is 6.49.)

items.q: Estimate 0.24 × 159.
items.e: 0.24 is close to 0.25. A quarter of 160 is 40. (The exact answer is 38.16.)

items.q: Estimate 25% of $79.
items.e: $79 is close to $80. 25% is one quarter: $80 ÷ 4 = $20. (The exact answer is $19.75.)

items.q: Estimate 50% of 198.
items.e: 198 is close to 200. 50% is one half: 200 ÷ 2 = 100. (The exact answer is 99.)

items.q: Estimate 10% of $61.
items.e: $61 is close to $60. 10% is one tenth: $60 ÷ 10 = $6. (The exact answer is $6.10.)

items.q: Estimate 9% of 412 by using 10% of 400.
items.e: 9% is close to 10%, and 412 is close to 400. 10% of 400 = 400 ÷ 10 = 40. (The exact answer is 37.08. 9% does not mean divide by 9.)

items.q: Estimate 75% of $41.
items.e: $41 is close to $40. 25% of $40 is $10, so 75% is 3 × $10 = $30. (The exact answer is $30.75.)

items.q: Estimate 20% of $148.
items.e: $148 is close to $150. 10% of $150 is $15, so 20% is 2 × $15 = $30. (The exact answer is $29.60.)

items.q: Estimate 49% of 803.
items.e: 49% is close to 50%, and 803 is close to 800. Half of 800 is 400. (The exact answer is 393.47.)

items.q: Estimate 1% of $2995.
items.e: $2995 is close to $3000. 1% is one hundredth: $3000 ÷ 100 = $30. (The exact answer is $29.95.)

items.q: Estimate 5% of $199.
items.e: $199 is close to $200. 10% of $200 is $20, so 5% is half of that: $10. (The exact answer is $9.95. 5% does not mean divide by 5.)

items.q: Estimate 24% of 121 kg.
items.e: 24% is close to 25%, and 121 kg is close to 120 kg. 120 kg ÷ 4 = 30 kg. (The exact answer is 29.04 kg.)

items.q: A jacket costs $59.95. It is 30% off. About how much do you save?
items.e: $59.95 is close to $60. 10% of $60 is $6, so 30% is 3 × $6 = $18. (The exact saving is $17.99. $42 would be the sale price, not the saving.)

items.q: Runners cost $119. They are 25% off. About how much is the sale price?
items.e: $119 is close to $120. 25% of $120 is $30, so the sale price is about $120 − $30 = $90. (The exact sale price is $89.25.)

items.q: A video game costs $49.95. It is 40% off. About how much is the sale price?
items.e: $49.95 is close to $50. 40% of $50 is $20, so the sale price is about $50 − $20 = $30. (The exact sale price is $29.97.)

items.q: A wetsuit costs $81. It is 15% off. About how much do you save?
items.e: $81 is close to $80. 10% of $80 is $8 and 5% is $4, so 15% is $8 + $4 = $12. (The exact saving is $12.15.)

items.q: A school has 297 students. 52% of them walk to school. About how many students walk?
items.e: 52% is close to 50%, and 297 is close to 300. Half of 300 is 150. (The exact answer is about 154.)

items.q: At a school of 403 students, 24% play footy. About how many students play footy?
items.e: 24% is close to 25%, and 403 is close to 400. A quarter of 400 is 100. (The exact answer is about 97.)

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 33% of the 612 students swim in a race. About how many students is that?
items.e: 33% is about one third. 612 is close to 600, and one third of 600 is 200. (The exact answer is about 202.)

items.q: Charlotte has $495 in a bank account. The bank pays 5% interest a year. About how much interest does she earn in one year?
items.e: $495 is close to $500. 10% of $500 is $50, so 5% is half of that: $25. (The exact interest is $24.75.)

items.q: Which is more: 48% of $62 or 26% of $79?
items.e: 48% of $62 is about half of $60 = $30. 26% of $79 is about a quarter of $80 = $20. So 48% of $62 is more. (Exact: $29.76 and $20.54.)

items.q: Noah scores 19 out of 41 on a quiz. About what percentage is that?
items.e: 19 out of 41 is close to 20 out of 40, which is one half. One half = 50%. (The exact answer is about 46%.)

items.q: A calculator gives the digits 2356 for 3.8 × 6.2, but the decimal point is missing. Use an estimate to choose the answer.
items.e: Estimate: 4 × 6 = 24. Only 23.56 is close to that.

items.q: A calculator gives the digits 3285 for 4.5 × 7.3, but the decimal point is missing. Use an estimate to choose the answer.
items.e: Estimate: 5 × 7 = 35. Only 32.85 is close to that.

items.q: A calculator gives the digits 291 for 0.6 × 48.5, but the decimal point is missing. Use an estimate to choose the answer.
items.e: Estimate: 0.6 × 50 = 30. Only 29.1 is close to that.

items.q: A calculator gives the digits 3224 for 12.4 × 2.6, but the decimal point is missing. Use an estimate to choose the answer.
items.e: Estimate: 12 × 3 = 36. Only 32.24 is close to that.

items.q: A calculator gives the digits 81 for 56.7 ÷ 7, but the decimal point is missing. Use an estimate to choose the answer.
items.e: Estimate: 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Only 8.1 is close to that.

items.q: Zara works out 4.9 × 6.1 and gets 298.9. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 5 × 6 = 30. 298.9 is not close to 30, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 29.89; the point is in the wrong place.

items.q: Grace works out 7.85 + 3.4 and gets 8.19. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 8 + 3 = 11. 8.19 is not close to 11, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 11.25. Line up the decimal points: 3.4 is 3 ones and 4 tenths, not 34 hundredths.

items.q: Aarav works out 12.6 − 4.85 and gets 7.75. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 13 − 5 = 8. 7.75 is close to 8, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Mei works out 8.2 × 3.9 and gets 31.98. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 8 × 4 = 32. 31.98 is close to 32, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Isla works out 45.6 ÷ 8 and gets 57. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 48 ÷ 8 = 6. 57 is not close to 6, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 5.7.

items.q: Sienna works out 25% of $82 and gets $41. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: a quarter of $80 is $20. $41 is not close to $20, so it is not reasonable. $41 is half of $82, which is 50%. The exact answer is $20.50.

items.q: Ava works out 10% of $67.50 and gets $6.75. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: one tenth of $70 is $7. $6.75 is close to $7, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Liam works out 6 × $14.95 and gets $89.70. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 6 × $15 = $90. $89.70 is close to $90, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 19.6 × 4.95?
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100. The exact answer is 97.02, so this estimate is the closest.

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 38.7 + 21.45 + 9.8?
items.e: 39 + 21 + 10 = 70. The exact answer is 69.95, so this estimate is the closest.

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 81.3 ÷ 9.2?
items.e: 81 ÷ 9 = 9. The exact answer is about 8.84, so this estimate is the closest.

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 0.52 × 297?
items.e: half of 300 = 150. The exact answer is 154.44, so this estimate is the closest.

items.q: Leo adds 2.4 m and 85 cm and gets 87.4 m. Is the answer reasonable?
c: Yes, it is close to 87 m
No, it should be about 3 m
Yes, the digits add up correctly
No, it should be about 87 cm
items.e: The units are different. 85 cm is less than 1 m (0.85 m). 2.4 m + 0.85 m is about 2 m + 1 m = 3 m, so 87.4 m is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3.25 m.

items.q: A bag of apples has a mass of 1.85 kg. Each apple is about 150 g. About how many apples are in the bag?
items.e: Use the same units: 1.85 kg = 1850 g. 1800 g ÷ 150 g = 12. (Dividing 1.85 by 150 mixes kilograms and grams.)

items.q: A recipe needs 750 mL of milk. Lachlan has a 2 L bottle that is about one quarter full. Does he have enough milk?
c: Yes, the bottle has about 2 L
No, the bottle has about 500 mL
No, the bottle has about 0.5 mL
Yes, the bottle has about 750 mL
items.e: 2 L = 2000 mL. One quarter of 2000 mL is 500 mL, and 500 mL is less than 750 mL, so no.

items.q: A 500 g bag of muesli costs $4.50. What is the price per 100 g?
A 2 kg bag of rice costs $5.80. What is the price per 100 g?
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g, which is 20 lots of 100 g. $5.80 ÷ 20 = 29c per 100 g. ($2.90 is the price per kilogram.)

items.q: Two packets of the same pasta are on sale. Which is the better buy?
c: the 750 g packet: it costs less
items.e: Compare the price of 100 g. 750 g: $6.00 ÷ 7.5 = 80c. 1 kg = 1000 g: $7.50 ÷ 10 = 75c. The 1 kg packet is the better buy.

items.q: A 1 kg tub of yoghurt costs $6.20. A 200 g pot costs $1.80. Which is the better buy?
c: the 200 g pot: it costs less
items.e: Use the same unit. 1 kg = 1000 g, so the tub is $6.20 ÷ 10 = 62c per 100 g. The pot is $1.80 ÷ 2 = 90c per 100 g. The 1 kg tub is the better buy.

items.q: Three boxes of the same cereal. Which box is the best buy?
c: They all cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Price per 100 g: 300 g: $3.90 ÷ 3 = $1.30. 500 g: $5.50 ÷ 5 = $1.10. 750 g: $8.40 ÷ 7.5 = $1.12. The 500 g box is the cheapest per 100 g. The biggest box is not always the best buy.

items.q: Matilda wants a bike that costs $289. She saves $18.50 every week. How many weeks does she need to save?
items.e: Estimate: $300 ÷ $20 = 15, so about 15 weeks. Check: 15 × $18.50 = $277.50, which is not enough. 16 × $18.50 = $296, so she needs 16 weeks.

items.q: Mia has $65. She wants a bike that costs $249 and saves $15 a week. How many more weeks does she need to save?
items.e: She still needs $249 − $65 = $184. $184 ÷ $15 is about 12.3. After 12 weeks she has saved $180, which is not enough, so she needs 13 weeks.

items.q: Year 6 has $120 for a class party. They buy 6 pizzas at $14.95 each and 4 bottles of juice at $3.80 each. Estimate. Is there enough money left for a $25 cake?
items.e: Pizzas: 6 × $15 = $90. Juice: 4 × $4 = $16. $90 + $16 = $106. $120 − $106 = $14, which is less than $25, so no. (Exactly $15.10 is left.)

items.q: Store A sells a skateboard for $79 with 25% off. Store B sells it for $65. Estimate. Which store is cheaper?
items.e: 25% of $80 is $20, so Store A charges about $80 − $20 = $60. $60 is less than $65, so Store A is cheaper. (The exact price is $59.25. $79 − $25 = $54 treats 25% as $25.)

items.q: A streaming service costs $14.99 a month. About how much does it cost for a year?
items.e: $14.99 rounds to $15, and a year has 12 months. 12 × $15 = $180. (The exact cost is $179.88.)

items.q: A car uses 7.8 L of petrol for every 100 km. About how much petrol does it use on a 290 km trip?
items.e: 290 km is about 3 lots of 100 km, and 7.8 L is about 8 L. 3 × 8 L = 24 L. (The exact amount is 22.62 L. 290 ÷ 7.8 ≈ 37 mixes up the units.)

items.q: Petrol costs $1.89 per litre. Dad puts 42 L in the car. About how much does he pay?
items.e: $1.89 is about $2, and 42 L is about 40 L. 40 × $2 = $80. (The exact cost is $79.38.)

items.q: Jack buys 3 beach towels at $12.95 each. The receipt says $388.50. Is that reasonable?
items.e: $12.95 is about $13. 3 × $13 = $39, so $388.50 is not reasonable. The exact total is $38.85; the point is in the wrong place.

items.q: Chloe gets $58 for her birthday and saves 25% of it. About how much does she save?
items.e: $58 is close to $60. 25% is one quarter: $60 ÷ 4 = $15. (The exact amount is $14.50.)

items.q: A bike costs $349. It is 20% off. About how much is the sale price?
items.e: $349 is close to $350. 10% of $350 is $35, so 20% is $70. $350 − $70 = $280. (The exact sale price is $279.20.)

items.q: Mum’s shopping costs $23.45, $18.90, $31.60, $12.85 and $9.70. Round each price to the nearest dollar. About how much is the total?
Year 6 sells 148 ice blocks at $2.95 each at the school fete. About how much money do they raise?
items.e: 148 is about 150 and $2.95 is about $3. 150 × $3 = $450. (The exact amount is $436.60.)

items.q: Kayak hire costs $28.50 per kayak for each hour. Oliver’s family hires 2 kayaks for 3 hours. About how much do they pay?
items.e: $28.50 is about $30. 2 kayaks for 3 hours is 2 × 3 = 6 kayak-hours. 6 × $30 = $180. (The exact cost is $171.)

items.q: Year 6 camp costs $385. Families can pay in 5 equal payments. About how much is each payment?
items.e: $385 is close to $400. $400 ÷ 5 = $80. (The exact payment is $77.)

items.q: Phone plan A costs $35 a month. Plan B costs $99 for 3 months. Which is cheaper for a whole year, and by how much?
items.e: Plan A: 12 × $35 = $420. Plan B: a year is 4 lots of 3 months, so 4 × $99 = $396. $420 − $396 = $24, so Plan B is cheaper by $24.
